name: Pap (ogi) with plain moi moi
why: Beans are a plant source of protein and iron. This moi moi has no egg or fish.
prep: Make the moi moi without egg or fish.

name: Boiled yam with ugu and tomato sauce
why: Leafy greens add iron, and tomatoes add vitamin C, which helps the body use iron from plants.

name: Boiled yam with vegetable egg sauce
why: Eggs add protein and leafy vegetables add iron.
prep: Cook the eggs until fully firm.

name: Oats with banana and milk
why: Oats and banana add fibre, and milk is a common source of calcium.
prep: Use pasteurised or well boiled milk.

name: Oats with banana and groundnuts
why: Oats and banana add fibre and groundnuts add protein.

name: Whole wheat bread with scrambled egg and tomato
why: A quick breakfast with protein, fibre and vitamin C from the tomato.
prep: Cook the eggs until fully firm.

name: Pap (ogi) with milk
why: Milk adds calcium and some protein to a light, easy breakfast.
prep: Use pasteurised or well boiled milk.

name: Boiled sweet potato with vegetable sauce
why: Sweet potato adds fibre and the vegetable sauce adds vitamins.

name: Ripe pawpaw
why: A cheap fruit with vitamin C and fibre.
prep: Choose fully ripe fruit only. Wash well and peel.

name: Orange or tangerine
why: A good source of vitamin C. Eat it with an iron-rich meal.
prep: Wash the fruit before peeling.

name: Watermelon slices
why: A refreshing fruit snack that helps with fluids.
prep: Wash the skin before cutting.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks
why: A crunchy vegetable snack with fibre.
prep: Wash well before eating.

name: Roasted groundnuts and banana
why: Groundnuts add protein and banana adds fruit.

name: Boiled egg with cucumber
why: A simple snack with protein and a vegetable.
prep: Boil the egg until fully firm.

name: Plain yoghurt with fruit
why: Yoghurt is a source of calcium and fruit adds fibre.
prep: Choose plain, pasteurised yoghurt.

name: Stewed beans with boiled plantain and vegetables
why: Beans are an affordable source of protein, iron and fibre.
prep: Cook beans until fully soft.

name: Yam and vegetable porridge
why: A filling meal with leafy vegetables, made without fish or meat.

name: Rice with sardine tomato sauce and vegetables
why: Canned sardines with soft bones can add calcium, and tomato adds vitamin C.
prep: Check the can label for other allergens.

name: Rice with tomato stew, grilled chicken and steamed vegetables
why: Balanced meal with protein, vegetables and vitamin C from the tomato stew.
prep: Cook chicken thoroughly until no pink remains.

name: Vegetable soup with fish and swallow
why: Leafy vegetables add iron and fish adds protein.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly. Made without crayfish.

name: Vegetable soup with beef and crayfish, and swallow
why: Leafy vegetables and meat both add iron, and meat adds protein.
prep: Cook meat thoroughly.

name: Egusi soup with leafy vegetables and fish
why: Egusi seeds and fish add protein and the leafy vegetables add iron.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly. Made without crayfish.

name: Jollof rice with plain moi moi and salad
why: Moi moi adds plant protein and iron and the salad adds vitamin C.
prep: Make the moi moi without egg or fish. Wash salad vegetables well.

name: Yam porridge with vegetables and fish
why: A one-pot meal with protein from fish and iron from leafy vegetables.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly.

name: Okra soup with fish and swallow
why: Okra adds vegetables and fibre and fish adds protein.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly. Made without crayfish.

name: Rice with soya chunks stew and vegetables
why: Soya chunks are a meat-free source of protein and iron.

name: Brown rice with stewed beans and steamed vegetables
why: Beans and brown rice together give protein, iron and fibre.

name: Boiled yam with pork stew and steamed vegetables
why: Meat adds protein and iron and the vegetables add fibre.
prep: Cook pork thoroughly until no pink remains.
